title: The text discusses the complex relationship between Israel and South Africa during the apartheid era, highlighting Israel's strategic defense ties with Pretoria and the efforts of Israeli officials to counter international criticism. It outlines a two-pronged approach: first, to create a compelling narrative that diminishes the significance of apartheid, and second, to defend Israel's actions by comparing them to those of other nations. Key figures, including Israeli Defense Minister Yitzhak Rabin and Julius Weinstein of the South African Zionist Federation, express concerns about the impact of international sanctions on both countries. The text also notes the South African Jewish community's discontent with the apartheid regime and the government's dismissal of their concerns, while revealing that other nations, including Saudi Arabia and Jordan, have been involved in arms dealings with South Africa.
